omitted.what: pre-treatment questions GSU201 (trust in government), GSU202 (run by a few big interests) with its follow-up GSU202x, and GSU203 (tax waste), asked before the crooked question
omitted.label: missing
omitted.why: the 2012 wording is not public: the authors' draft (ccap) prints a trust stem with three alternatives and 3 options, a 3-option waste stem and no follow-up, while the YouGov codebook proves the fielded items had 5 options (GSU201: Just about always ... Hardly at all), a follow-up (GSU202x labels 'Run by a few big interests - Just about always' ..., asked of 1964 of 2000) and 4 options (GSU203: Almost all tax money is wasted ...). Serving the draft or the 2020 replication's wording would fill the gap with plausible text. Evidence they were fielded: codebook variables GSU201, GSU202, GSU202x, GSU203 with counts (pp. 126-127). Priming consequence: meta.conflicts 'pre-treatment priming absent'
fielded text not public (draft text carries drafting notes); no codebook variable

score_replication_61k8.why: different instrument and sample (Qualtrics 2020, no control condition, crooked blocks merged to 3, pandemic onset); not built as an arm in this conversion

unsupported.why: weights depend on the realised block counts and YouGov's panel weights; every outcome item scores the unweighted value (printed on p. 23 or derived exactly from it), the weighted ones are kept as estimates; recall items score the IPW values (the only ones printed), see meta.scope

keyed.why: answers that make the paper's pattern true: innuendo lowers favorability and raises belief in bribery and the investigation; the denial repairs part of it; the causal correction most of it

answers.inv.inv: choice([1, 2]) if cond == 'innuendo' else choice([2, 3]) if cond == 'denial' else choice([3, 4])
answers.bribes.bribes: choice([4, 5]) if cond == 'control' else choice([1, 2]) if cond == 'innuendo' else choice([2, 3]) if cond == 'denial' else choice([3, 4])
